content: Partner 1 claimed co‑ownership of properties bought during marriage despite an “adhesive intervention” where she confirmed the price derived from Partner 2’s personal assets (art. 179 c.c.). The core issue was whether that spouse’s declaration is merely an intention or a confession of historical fact requiring revocation for error/violence. The court framed the case under art. 179 and Supreme Court guidance distinguishing personal assets by origin vs. use. Interpretively, a declaration confirming the personal origin of the price is confessional and binds unless revoked under art. 2732 c.c. Principles: absent proof of error or coercion, the asset remains personal and excluded from community; mere references to art. 179 without factual content differ. Costs were awarded against the unsuccessful plaintiff.
